entry.title: Thin-Shell Wormholes in Born--Infeld-Type Magnetic Spacetimes
entry.summary: We investigate the radial stability, thermodynamic balance, and bilateral disk images of symmetric thin-shell wormholes built from Born--Infeld-type magnetic exteriors. The exact lapse and junction conditions define a fixed-mass family in which magnetic self-energy ties the nonlinear scale to the charge. The shell has negative energy density, although an inner sampled region satisfies the tangential null and intrinsic strong energy conditions. Linear radial perturbations yield unstable calibrated barotropic samples and stable sectors for the generalized and modified cosmic Chaplygin laws on selected real branches. Analytic horizon and large-radius limits explain the stability transitions and show how the modified linear pressure term can replace outer stability with finite radial intervals. Minimally coupled Maxwell rays traverse transparent junctions between exteriors with a common arctangent emission profile, viewed by a static observer. The wormhole-black-hole intensity difference separates transmitted disk light from emission removed by throat excision. Compared with static emitters, circular and plunging motion reduce the face-on intensities in the studied cases; inclined motion generates strong azimuthal contrast. Increasing the subcritical charge contracts the critical circle and permits more disk crossings near it in the optical samples. Under a reversible first law, flux cancellation gives isentropic motion at positive temperature, with entropy dependence left to a constitutive completion. These results distinguish geometric, material, and kinematic effects on shell support and disk illumination.

entry.title: Neural Network Fractional Quantum Hall States with Learnable Orbital Pair Matrix Factors: Balancing Physical Priors and Flexibility
entry.summary: Neural network fractional quantum Hall (FQH) states offer a promising alternative for capturing Landau level (LL) mixing and for understanding FQH physics, yet the incorporation of physical priors has so far been limited to the minimal exact constraints built into the ansatz. Working in spherical geometry, we show that the network's flexibility suffers both when only minimal additional physical priors are supplied and when priors such as flux attachment are imposed rigidly. In the former case, the monopole harmonic product orbital (MHPO) ansatz is difficult to optimize, whereas in the latter, the expressivity of the neural network is restricted. We therefore propose the orbital pair matrix factor MHPO (MHPO-M) ansatz, which balances physical priors against flexibility by not only replacing the fixed Laughlin structure with learnable pair factors but also making them dependent on both the electron configurations and the orbitals. Across $ν=1/5$, $1/3$, and $2/5$, MHPO-M achieves the lowest variational energy among the tested variants, and a factorized orbital readout based on it enables scaling to 35 electrons, with energies competitive with trends inferred from three-LL exact-diagonalization results. These results demonstrate that physical priors can be appropriately incorporated without sacrificing the flexibility of neural network wavefunctions, opening a promising path toward accurate, scalable modeling of FQH systems with LL mixing.

entry.title: Pulsar J1909+0749 and Supernova Remnant G42.1-0.2: A case of a pulsar that has exited the shell of its associated supernova remnant
entry.summary: (Abridged) The ATNF pulsar catalogue features only 63 pulsars that are possibly associated with a supernova remnant (SNR). Even rarer is the scenario in which the pulsar has escaped the physical extent of its corresponding SNR. We aim to identify the serendipitously discovered shell-type object G42.1-0.2 as a SNR. The known pulsar (PSR) J1909+0749 lies well outside the shell of SNR G42.1-0.2, but it has a cometary tail pointing towards the centre of the SNR; we propose that the SNR and the pulsar originated from the same supernova explosion. By measuring the flux densities of the shell G42.1-0.2 from ${\sim}$200 MHz to ${\sim}$6 GHz, we establish the nonthermal nature of its emission. With the characteristic age of the pulsar, its distance from the Sun estimated from the dispersion measure (DM), and the angular separation between the pulsar and the centre of the shell, we infer the evolutionary state of the SNR and the transverse velocity of the pulsar. Using proper motion measurements, we compare the SNR-pulsar direction with the velocity of the pulsar. The radio spectral index of the shell is $-0.36 \pm 0.08$, confirming that the emission is primarily nonthermal synchrotron. The proper motion measurements are not well constrained, but the amplitude and the direction are consistent with the interpretation that the SNR and the pulsar are associated. If the characteristic age and the DM-based distance represent the true age and the true distance of the pulsar and the SNR, then the standard evolution equations suggest that the SNR must still be in the Sedov-Taylor phase, evolving in a medium with a density of about 1.5 cm$^{-3}$. In addition, as a result of the PSR-SNR association, the transverse velocity of the pulsar PSR J1909+0749 is estimated to be ${\sim}1460~\mathrm{km\,s}^{-1}$, ranking it among the highest transverse velocities observed for pulsars in the Milky Way.

entry.title: Constraints on Dark Matter Annihilation from Starlight-Induced Inverse Compton Emission in Omega Centauri
entry.summary: The search for the particle identity of dark matter (DM) remains one of the foremost challenges in modern physics. In this work, we derive new constraints on the DM annihilation cross section $\langleσv\rangle$ by considering the inverse Compton (IC) scattering of DM annihilation injected $e^+e^-$ off the starlight radiation field in Omega Centauri. As a likely remnant core of a dwarf galaxy, Omega Centauri provides a dense stellar environment that enhances the predict IC signal. Using multi-wavelength observations from Chandra and Fermi-LAT, we establish upper limits on $\langleσv\rangle$ over a wide DM mass range from MeV to TeV. Notably, in the tens-of-MeV range, our results surpass existing constraints by approximately two orders of magnitude, exceeding $\langleσv\rangle \sim 10^{-31}~{\rm cm^3\,s^{-1}}$. At several GeV to the TeV DM masses range, our constraints also remain stronger than existing limits. Our results demonstrate that starlight induced IC emission is an important component for indirect DM searches in dense stellar systems, establishing Omega Centauri as a powerful probe of the nature of DM.

entry.title: The Topological Multiverse as the Self-Consistent Extension of Everettian QM to Quantum Gravity
entry.summary: The ``fine-tuning" of the fundamental constants, from the cosmological constant to the gauge structure of the Standard Model, suggests that our universe inhabits a rare, life-permitting island within a vast landscape of theoretical possibilities. We argue that this landscape arises as a self-consistent extension of Everettian quantum mechanics, once the Wheeler--DeWitt path integral is allowed to sum over admissible topologies rather than being restricted to a single background. Enlarging the DeWitt sum of geometries to include all smooth manifolds supporting causal dynamics promotes the dimensionality, gauge groups, and coupling constants from fixed background inputs to dynamical variables of the sum. Spacetime is admitted only where metric elements sustain an extended differentiable Lorentzian geometry. Omnipresent quantum metric fluctuations, combined with curvature-induced deformation, can drive a substantial fraction of elementary regions outside the nondegenerate Lorentzian class. Under the adopted admissibility condition, these regions are absent from the physical manifold and constitute quantum topological holes (QTHs). A quantum boundary $\mathcal{B}_Q$ occurs in collapse when the surviving Lorentzian regions lose the connectivity required for an extended differentiable spacetime; in the time-reversed expanding interpretation, it marks the onset of admissible spacetime rather than emergence from a singularity or a pre-geometric foam. At $\mathcal{B}_Q$, the integral generates a coherent superposition of distinct topologies that branch into disjoint U-sectors, each governed by its own effective field theory, with inter-sector transitions dynamically frozen shortly after nucleation. The topological multiverse is, in this view, not imposed but implicit in the quantum mechanics revealed by the sum over geometries.

entry.title: Reconstructing the Goldberg-Palatini Action from Noether Identities
entry.summary: We investigate the reconstruction of the first-order gravitational action from the Noether identities associated with diffeomorphism invariance. The independent fields are a symmetric perturbation $φ^{μν}$ of the contravariant metric density and a trace-adjusted connection $G^λ{}_{μν}$, whose transformation laws are prescribed. For a local action polynomial in these fields, with the gravitational coupling as its only dimensionful constant and each additional field carrying one power of it, a dilatation, which is a particular diffeomorphism, shows that in any dimension $d>2$ the action terminates at most at cubic order, its only possible cubic term being a derivative-free $φGG$ vertex. Expanding the kernels of the resulting Lorentz-covariant ansatz in tensor bases gives 31 coefficients for $d\geq 4$. The Noether identities with general diffeomorphisms, expanded order by order in the fields, yield a linear system that eliminates the $φφ$ kernel and determines the remaining coefficients up to an overall normalization, recovering the Goldberg-Palatini action. Since the connection can be eliminated exactly, this also fixes the complete second-order action, with its infinite set of graviton vertices. The construction requires no choice of energy-momentum tensor, the source of ambiguity in the self-coupling approach. The kernel bases, the identities and the solution are given in appendices, and the symbolic computations are publicly available.

entry.title: Direction-dependent magnetoelectric conductivity from dipolar topological semimetals
entry.summary: We compute the linear magnetoelectric conductivity of a two-band vortex nodal-ring (VNR) semimetal and a three-band Hopf semimetal (HSM) within the semiclassical Boltzmann formalism, in the relaxation-time approximation, for three inequivalent planar-Hall configurations, with the electric ($\boldsymbol E$) and magnetic ($\boldsymbol B$) fields oriented differently relative to the nodal-ring plane and the Berry-curvature (BC) dipole axis. Unlike Weyl and multifold semimetals with point-monopole BC flux, the HSM carries a single, point-like BC-dipole fixed at its node, while the VNR hosts a continuous ring of such sources around the nodal loop. Both have vanishing Chern numbers. Working consistently to cubic order in $\boldsymbol B$, we evaluate the Drude, BC, orbital-magnetic-moment (OMM), anomalous-Hall, and Lorentz-force contributions. In both systems, the dipolar BC and OMM activate out-of-plane and odd-in-$\boldsymbol B$ in-plane response-channels that are symmetry-forbidden for a BC-monopole. Mirror symmetry confines the odd longitudinal terms to $B_z$, the field component along the dipole axis. The internode-scattering conductivity of the HSM vanishes identically, since the dipolar BC and OMM are even in momentum and no charge is pumped between two conjugate Hopf nodes, which carry oppositely oriented BC-dipoles. Comparisons with a $\mathcal{PT}$-broken gapped nodal-ring and a pseudospin-1 triple-point semimetal confirm the dipolar-BC origin of these features.

entry.title: Time-Reversal Symmetry in Artificial Topological Graphene Rings
entry.summary: We study an artificial graphene ring described by the low-energy two-valley Dirac Hamiltonian with a uniform mass term. When the ring is threaded by an Aharonov-Bohm flux, the problem reduces to a second-order radial equation solved by Bessel functions. We give the exact secular equation and, for narrow rings, closed expressions for the spectrum and the persistent current. We then add a uniform magnetic field perpendicular to the plane. The radial problem is solved with confluent hypergeometric functions, and the persistent current and magnetization are written as derivatives of a secular determinant from which the spurious roots have been removed. Besides the usual orbital coupling, the field enters through a valley-dependent term that comes from the Dirac structure and lifts the valley degeneracy. A weak-field expansion, accurate up to corrections of order B^4, gives this valley splitting explicitly and separates the diamagnetic and paramagnetic contributions to the susceptibility. Finally, we work out what time reversal implies for the spectrum. Physical time reversal, which exchanges the valleys, leads to an exact relation between levels at opposite fields. The effective single-valley time reversal, on the other hand, is broken by the mass term and by the boundary conditions, yet leaves no trace in the zero-field spectrum. Numerical results for the spectrum, the persistent current, and the magnetization illustrate the analysis.

entry.title: On the superbursts as photodisintegrators of ashes from the rp-process -- Numerical simulations of superbursts with MESA II
entry.summary: Context: Superbursts are energetic explosions in the crusts of neutron stars in Low-Mass X-ray Binaries (LMXBs). At temperatures above 4 GK, photodisintegration of heavy rp-process ashes may play a major role alongside $^{12}$C fusion. Aims: We investigate how photodisintegration of rp-process ashes affects superburst properties and the initial $^{12}$C abundance required for ignition. Methods: We simulate superbursts with MESA v.24.08.1. Besides the canonical fuel of $20\%$ $^{12}$C and $80\%$ $^{56}$Fe, we test different $^{12}$C abundances mixed with scaled rp-process ashes. Results: Superbursts can ignite with only $10\%$ $^{12}$C when the remaining $90\%$ consists of rp-process ashes. Their luminosity is comparable to that of the canonical fuel, whereas $10\%$ $^{12}$C mixed with $90\%$ $^{56}$Fe yields lower luminosity. $^{56}$Fe remains the most abundant ash nuclide. Although photodisintegration drives nucleosynthesis, neutron, proton and alpha captures release energy at late times. We also find that $A=64$ nuclides or $^{20}$Ne help reduce the $^{12}$C abundance needed for ignition. Conclusions: The composition of accreted material - not just its $^{12}$C content - substantially affects superburst ignition, luminosity and nucleosynthesis.

entry.title: Contrasting Crystal-Field and Dipolar Anisotropies in the Triangular Antiferromagnet NaBaEr(BO$_3$)$_2$
entry.summary: The magnetic ground states of rare-earth frustrated magnets can be governed by competing energy scales arising from crystal-field anisotropy, exchange interactions, and long-range dipolar interactions. Here we investigate this interplay in the triangular-lattice antiferromagnet NaBaEr(BO$_3$)$_2$ by combining magnetization, specific heat, and neutron scattering measurements. Neutron powder diffraction resolves rotations of the ErO$_6$ octahedra and supports the lower-symmetry $R\bar{3}$ structure over the previously proposed $R\bar{3}m$ model. Magnetization measurements and inelastic neutron scattering establish an effective spin-1/2 description of its low-temperature magnetism with pronounced easy-axis anisotropy, arising from a well-isolated Kramers ground-state doublet separated from the first excited crystal-electric-field level by approximately 4 meV. Below $T_{\rm N}=0.1$ K, single-crystal neutron diffraction reveals A-type antiferromagnetic order with the ordered moment predominantly oriented within the $ab$ plane, despite the pronounced paramagnetic easy-axis anisotropy. The estimated dipolar interaction scale is comparable to $T_{\rm N}$, and classical dipolar-energy calculations for the observed stacking pattern favor an in-plane moment orientation. These results reveal contrasting crystal-field and dipolar anisotropies in determining the magnetic ground state of NaBaEr(BO$_3$)$_2$.

entry.title: Rare-earth tuning of magnetic entropy and interaction scales in K$_3$$Ln$(PO$_4$)$_2$ ($Ln$ = Yb, Gd) for adiabatic demagnetization refrigeration
entry.summary: Adiabatic demagnetization refrigeration (ADR) based on frustrated rare-earth magnets provides a promising route toward helium-free sub-Kelvin cooling, while balancing magnetic entropy and interaction scales is essential for optimizing the ADR functionalities. Here we investigate the low-temperature magnetic and ADR properties of the alkali rare-earth double phosphates K$_3$$Ln$(PO$_4$)$_2$ ($Ln$ = Yb, Gd), which crystallize in a monoclinic $P2_1/m$ structure containing distorted isosceles triangular lattices of rare-earth ions. Magnetization and specific heat measurements confirm the absence of long-range magnetic ordering down to 0.1 K in both compounds. Direct quasi-ADR measurements demonstrate strongly contrasting refrigeration behaviors: K$_3$Yb(PO$_4$)$_2$ reaches a minimum temperature of 29.8 mK from an initial state of 2 K and 6 T, whereas K$_3$Gd(PO$_4$)$_2$ exhibits extended hold times below 150 mK associated with its larger magnetic entropy reservoir. Crystal-electric-field calculations confirm a $J_{\mathrm{eff}} = 1/2$ ground-state doublet in K$_3$Yb(PO$_4$)$_2$, while thermodynamic analysis based on magnetic entropy and interaction scales accounts for the distinct ADR performance of the two compounds. These results identify K$_3$$Ln$(PO$_4$)$_2$ as a chemically robust platform for rare-earth-tunable solid-state ADR.

entry.title: Rapid Variability of Radiative Signatures from Driven Relativistic Reconnection
entry.summary: Rapid variability in energetic flares is a distinctive feature of high-energy emission from many magnetically dominated astrophysical sources. We investigate the radiative variability of driven relativistic magnetic reconnection using Particle-in-Cell simulations of strongly magnetized flux tubes pushed to merge at driving speed $v_{\rm push}$. This setup captures the onset of reconnection and provides a controlled model for single reconnection-driven flares near compact objects, where magnetic structures can be twisted, sheared, and forced to merge by turbulent accretion flows or relativistic frame dragging. We find that the merger efficiently accelerates particles into nonthermal distributions, producing synchrotron emission whose variability tracks the reconnection phases. We identify two regimes: a quasi-steady, weakly driven regime for $v_{push}\leq0.1\,c$, and strongly driven regime for $v_{\rm push}>0.1\,c$. The transition occurs when the driving exceeds the typical inflow-to-outflow velocity ratio of $\sim0.1$ in steady collisionless relativistic reconnection, i.e., the average rate at which reconnection can process incoming flux, potentially providing an additional source of variability. The lightcurves rise on $1$--$3$ light-crossing times of the reconnecting region, and the particle spectra develop power laws with index $p\simeq1.8$--$2.4$. These timescales are compatible with observed variability in high-energy sources, including the very-high-energy flares of M87$^*$ and the $γ$-ray flares of the Crab Nebula, making this model a viable framework for rapid flaring in active galactic nuclei and pulsar wind nebulae.

entry.title: A Concentration of Measure Phenomenon in the Principal Chiral Model
entry.summary: We utilize the concentration of measure phenomenon to study the double limit (large-$N$ and continuum) of the $O(N)$ principal chiral model, where the large-$N$ limit is performed before the continuum one. The partition function in this double limit is demonstrated to be that of a free massive theory. The result depends crucially on the order in which the limits are taken.

entry.title: Heavy holographic correlators in defect conformal field theories
entry.summary: We study holographic defect conformal field theories which are dual to probe branes with bottom-up methods. First we determine the embedding of codimension-1 interface branes in AdS space. Then we compute defect one and two-point functions of heavy scalar operators at strong coupling. We use geodesic approximations to compute reflected two-point functions in two ways, as well as ambient and defect-channel two-point functions. In appropriate limits, our results agree with the operator product expansion (OPE) and the boundary operator expansion (BOE).

entry.title: Dark Energy Survey Year 6 Results: improved mitigation of spatially varying observational systematics with masking for the MagLim++ lens sample
entry.summary: As photometric surveys reach unprecedented statistical precision, systematic uncertainties increasingly dominate large-scale structure probes relying on galaxy number density. Defining the final survey footprint is critical, as it excludes regions affected by artefacts or suboptimal observing conditions. For galaxy clustering, spatially varying observational systematics, such as seeing, are a leading source of bias. Template maps of contaminants are used to derive spatially dependent corrections, but extreme values may fall outside the applicability range of mitigation methods, compromising correction reliability. The complexity and accuracy of systematics modelling depend on footprint conservativeness, with aggressive masking enabling simpler, robust mitigation. We present a unified approach to define the DES Y6 JOINT footprint, integrating observational systematics templates and artefact indicators that degrade mitigation performance. This removes extreme values from an initial SEED footprint, leading to the final JOINT footprint. By evaluating the DES Y6 lens sample MagLim++ on this footprint, we enhance the Iterative Systematics Decontamination (ISD) method, detecting non-linear systematic contamination and improving correction accuracy. While the mask's impact on clustering is less significant than systematics decontamination, it remains non-negligible, comparable to statistical uncertainties in certain w(theta) scales and redshift bins. Supporting coherent analyses of galaxy clustering and cosmic shear, the final footprint spans 4,031.04 deg2, setting the basis for DES Y6 1x2pt, 2x2pt, and 3x2pt analyses. This work highlights how targeted masking strategies optimise the balance between statistical power and systematic control in Stage-III and -IV surveys.

entry.title: Direct Urca process facilitated by non-Fermi-liquid quantum criticality
entry.summary: Conventional Fermi-liquid theories of dense nuclear matter predict that the direct Urca process requires a proton fraction above a threshold of $Y_p \approx 0.11$--$0.15$, which is rarely reached in low-mass neutron stars. Here we show that this stringent kinematic constraint is drastically relaxed by the non-Fermi liquid behavior arising from superfluid and superconducting quantum criticality in neutron stars. In the non-Fermi-liquid regimes, nucleons have a smooth momentum occupation without a sharp Fermi surface, and their chemical potentials develop a logarithmic temperature dependence. These intrinsic features fundamentally alter the standard $β$-equilibrium relation. Consequently, direct Urca neutrino emission can be activated even at low nuclear densities. This modifies the long-standing Urca-threshold paradigm and indicates that direct Urca process has the opportunity to occur in low-mass neutron stars.

entry.title: Two-Component Dark Matter and Strongly First-Order Electroweak Phase Transition via a Two-Step Mechanism in the Inert Doublet plus Real Singlet Model
entry.summary: We study a two-component dark matter model in which a real singlet scalar and an inert doublet scalar are simultaneously present alongside the Standard Model, each stabilized by an independent discrete symmetry. The real singlet undergoes a strong first-order transition at high temperature, establishing an intermediate phase with a non-zero singlet vacuum expectation value, which in turn generates the barrier required for the Higgs field to complete a strongly first-order electroweak transition at a lower temperature. This two-step mechanism naturally enforces the condition $v_c/T_c \geq 1$, the sphaleron washout-avoidance criterion necessary for electroweak baryogenesis. The gravitational wave spectrum from both steps is computed; the second step produces a decihertz signal, peaking near $0.08$--$0.34~\mathrm{Hz}$ across the viable parameter space and $0.14$--$0.22~\mathrm{Hz}$ at the benchmark points, that reaches the sensitivity of DECIGO for the strongest transitions and of BBO more widely, while the first remains sub-threshold for all planned detectors. At the coupling values required to drive the phase transition, the singlet is generically underabundant as a thermal relic, so the inert doublet carries the dominant fraction of the observed relic density. Confronting the model with current constraints, we find that the LUX-ZEPLIN 2024 result excludes the entire electroweak-phase-transition-viable parameter space of the singlet sector across the full mass range, even after rescaling by the singlet relic fraction, establishing a complete no-go for the singlet as a viable thermal dark matter candidate in this framework.

entry.title: Kinematically isolating intracluster light in AS1063: a distinct stellar population tracing the dark matter core
entry.summary: We present a technique using integral-field spectroscopy to kinematically isolate intracluster light (ICL) from the brightest cluster galaxy (BCG), enabling insights into their contrasting stellar populations and the inner dark matter halo profile. Applying this technique to MUSE data of Abell S1063, we find that both components are old (~9 Gyr), but the ICL is more metal-poor than the BCG, implying distinct progenitor pathways. Within 100 kpc, the ICL comprises 55 per cent of the BCG+ICL stellar mass - substantially more than inferred from photometric decompositions. The BCG and ICL possess distinct velocity distributions, which remain nearly constant with radius, with an ICL velocity dispersion more than twice that of the BCG, and a line-of-sight velocity offset of 86 +- 18 km/s. Two-dimensional Sérsic fits yield an ICL centroid offset of 5.2 +- 1.5 kpc from the BCG. These phase-space offsets are indicative of the BCG oscillating in a broad potential minimum. Furthermore, the ICL surface-brightness profile matches that of strong-lensing estimates assuming a cored halo. Simulations indicate that the inner halo profile varies systematically for different dark matter models. Applied to larger samples, our method therefore offers a complementary route to testing the nature of dark matter, while simultaneously revealing the stellar origins of the ICL.

entry.title: The Continuum Limit Analysis of Causal Fermion Systems for Curved Spacetimes
entry.summary: We construct the causal fermion system for globally hyperbolic spacetimes starting in the framework of algebraic quantum field theory. The fermionic projector is identified with the one-particle density operator of a quasi-free Hadamard state. The ultraviolet regularization is built into the fermionic projector via a chart-independent $i\varepsilon$-regularization scheme. The continuum limit analysis is developed in globally hyperbolic spacetimes. It is shown that the Euler-Lagrange equations of the causal action principle are satisfied in this setup if and only if the coupled Einstein-Dirac equations hold.

entry.title: Interacting quantum criticality with U(1) symmetry breaking in 1+1 dimensions
entry.summary: The Hohenberg-Mermin-Wagner theorem motivates the expectation that continuous symmetry remains unbroken in one-dimensional quantum ground states. Here, contrary to this expectation, we demonstrate the spontaneous breaking of U(1) spin-rotation symmetry and the emergence of an interacting quantum critical point in lattice spin-$1/2$ and spin-$1$ chains. Using subsystem Binder scaling, we locate the critical point and determine the correlation-length critical exponent as $ν= 0.60 \pm 0.02$, distinct from the Gaussian value $1/2$ but consistent with the perturbative renormalization-group value. We further estimate the dynamical critical exponent to be $z = 1.986 \pm 0.005$ from the lowest neutral excitation gap and $z = 1.955 \pm 0.021$ from the longitudinal spin correlations. The results $z < 2$ are incompatible with microscopic realizations of this critical theory by frustration-free models, implying a mechanism for continuous symmetry breaking in one-dimensional quantum ground states distinct from frustration freeness.

entry.title: Synthesis and stability of high-$T_c$ LaH$_{10\pmδ}$ films at high pressures
entry.summary: High-pressure hydrides hold the record for the highest superconducting critical temperatures across all classes of superconductors. Currently lanthanum decahydride, LaH$_{10}$, exhibits the highest critical temperature among binaries, with $T_c \approx$ 250 K at pressures between 140-180 GPa. Here, we report the synthesis of LaH$_{10\pmδ}$ films in two DACs at pressures of 168 GPa and 176 GPa via in situ laser heating of elemental lanthanum films with ammonia borane (NH$_3$BH$_3$) as the hydrogen donor. The high-symmetry fcc lanthanum sublattice (space group $Fm\bar3m$) is resolved using synchrotron X-ray diffraction, with unit cell parameters in excellent agreement with previous studies on bulk samples. We provide confirmation of high-$T_c$ superconductivity in LaH$_{10\pmδ}$ with highest $T_c$ of 247 K at 176 GPa evidenced in electrical measurements. The characteristic suppression of superconductivity is observed in magnetic fields. Furthermore, combined diffraction and electrical measurements reveal remarkable temporal stability of both the crystal structure and the high-$T_c$ superconductivity over the full measurement period of about 300 days post laser heating. Our work establishes film precursors using physical vapour deposition (PVD) techniques as a practical route to hydride formation, opening a pathway toward the controlled synthesis of promising ternary hydrides and the integration of micro-fabricated device geometries in diamond anvil cells.

entry.title: Non-minimal unimodular inflation revisited: Swampland diagnostics and CMB constraints
entry.summary: We study non-minimal unimodular inflation in the Einstein frame; the effective potential takes the form $U(\varphi)=U_0(1+ξ\varphi^2/\mpl^2)^{-2}$. We consider the canonical field map and the inflationary observables directly from the Einstein-frame action. The exact potential slow-roll parameters, the leading scalar running, the scalar-amplitude normalization, the e-fold relation, and the end-of-inflation condition are obtained analytically. The model has a nontrivial structural tension: an $ε_V=1$ exit requires $ξ>1/2$, whereas the near-origin slow-roll regime requires $ξ\ll1$ and gives $n_s\simeq1-8ξ$. We next test three distinct swampland diagnostics. The further-refined de Sitter conjecture (FRDSSC) introduces the independent conjectural parameters $a$, $b$, and $q$, while the scalar weak gravity conjecture (SWGC) and its strong form (SSWGC) contain no analogous tunable conjecture parameter in the single-field realization adopted here. All three criteria are evaluated using the canonically normalized Einstein-frame scalar. Analytic limits show that the SWGC is violated at the stationary point for every nonzero $ξ$, whereas the SSWGC at that point requires $ξ\gtrsim0.0643$. In the large-field limit both scalar weak-gravity diagnostics reduce to the same threshold $ξ\ge0.1$. Numerical scans then show that the observationally relevant ACT/P-ACT region does not satisfy either scalar weak-gravity criterion, while the FRDSSC can be satisfied for $a$ close to unity. Consequently, the minimal model can reproduce acceptable $(n_s,r)$ at isolated field values, but this does not constitute a complete 50-60 e-fold inflationary history or simultaneous satisfaction of all three conjectures.

entry.title: Adjusted Connections I: Differential Cocycles for Principal Groupoid Bundles with Connection
entry.summary: We develop a new perspective on principal bundles with connection as morphisms from the tangent bundle of the underlying manifold to a classifying dg-Lie groupoid. This groupoid can be identified with a lift of the inner homomorphisms groupoid arising in Ševera's differentiation procedure of Lie quasi-groupoids. Our new perspective readily extends to principal groupoid bundles, but requires an adjustment, an additional datum familiar from higher gauge theory. We show that for Lie groupoids, the additional adjustment data amounts to a Cartan connection. The resulting adjusted connections naturally provide a global formulation of the kinematical data of curved Yang-Mills-Higgs theories as described by Kotov-Strobl (arXiv:1510.07654) and Fischer (arXiv:2104.02175).

entry.title: QMBL: the Quantum Many-Body Leaderboard. A live record of published ground-state energies for lattice Hamiltonians and the electron gas
entry.summary: In condensed matter physics, scientists explore phase diagrams of matter through various methods (analysis, numerics, experiment) and achieve consensus when enough methods agree. The quality of variational results for quantum many-body ground states is mainly judged by energy values and respective errors. Here, we present QMBL, the Quantum Many-Body Leaderboard (https://www.qmbl.org), serving as the energy layer of the scientific consensus. It is a maintained, interactive record of published ground-state energies for lattice Hamiltonians and the homogeneous electron gas. The latest release v0.5.0 holds 2511 energies on 532 instances and collects all of the community's efforts into one view. Of those instances 285 have no exact solution (164 lattice and all 121 electron-gas instances) and any new record serves as a direct improvement to an open science problem. They are the targets of a companion benchmark, QMBL: Open Problems.

entry.title: Off-shell recursion for all-loop planar integrands in Yang-Mills theory
entry.summary: In this paper, we develop in detail the off-shell recursion for planar loop integrands in Yang-Mills theory. Starting from the classical equations of motion solved with the perturbiner method, we derive an exact transfer-matrix representation of the pure-gluon sector. We then include the ghost contributions to the loop kernels based on \cite{Tao:2025fch}. Finally, as an example, we work out the two-loop recursion in detail and conclude a general recursion strategy for two-loop planar integrands whose external legs are gluons.

entry.title: Néel Ordered Magnetic Phases in Bipartite Quasicrystals
entry.summary: Magnetism is a fundamental research area in which the recently proposed altermagnetism (AM) has become an emergent frontier. Very recently, the quasicrystal (QC) was proposed as a possible platform to realize AM. However, the existence of AM in QCs still lacks vigorous evidence. In this work, we adopt the sign-problem-free projector quantum Monte Carlo (PQMC) algorithm to investigate the magnetic phases in the half-filled Hubbard models in various 2D bipartite QCs, and always obtain Néel ordered states. While the Néel states in bipartite crystals are usually antiferromagnetism (AFM), we find it common that those in bipartite QCs can also be AM or ferrimagnetism (FIM). Based on symmetry analysis, combined with our comprehensive PQMC results, we propose a general criterion for determining the magnetism classes of the Néel states in a bipartite QC: According to whether the two sublattices are related by inversion, a non-inversion point-group operation such as mirror or rotation, or no operation about the unique symmetry center, the corresponding Néel state is AFM, AM or FIM / geometry-enforced AM (G-AM), respectively. The G-AM is a special type of $s$-wave AM caused by the unique QC structure formed through projection from high-dimensional crystals to lower dimensions, which is rare in crystals. For example, our results yield symmetry-protected AM for the two $D_4$-symmetric Thue-Morse QCs and G-AM for the $D_5$-symmetric Penrose QC at half-filling. Our results provide a solid foundation for experimental investigations and potential applications of different classes of magnetism in QCs.

entry.title: Local-Channel Stability of Classical $\mathbb Z_2$ Lattice Gauge Models
entry.summary: We establish sufficient conditions for two-way local quantum-channel stability in classical $\mathbb Z_2$ lattice gauge models with spins on $m$-dimensional cells of a $d$-dimensional lattice. Each interaction multiplies the spins on the boundary of an $(m+1)$-cell. This family, defined on the full spin Hilbert space without a Gauss-law constraint, includes the Ising model at $m=0$ and the magnetic sector of the toric code at $m=1$. The low-temperature proof combines two ingredients: locally indistinguishable flat sectors and extended magnetic defects of dimension $d-m-1$. For $1\le m\le d-2$, sufficiently weak local classical perturbations at sufficiently low positive temperature preserve equivalence to the canonical flat ensemble. No internal or gauge symmetry is required of the perturbation. For weak noncommuting perturbations, we prove the same conclusion in a smaller sufficient window by reducing the diagonal probabilities to a weak classical interaction and recovering the coherences with a local channel. The conversion channels use product ancillary inputs, have polylogarithmic causal radius, and achieve any prescribed inverse-power whole-system trace-norm error. Sufficiently high-temperature states are instead two-way equivalent to a product state. Independent finite-dimensional onsite systems can be included with weak local couplings. An optimized covariance between two distant neighborhoods of parallel $m$-tori is nonincreasing under one-way local conversion and invariant under two-way conversion. Its values $\mathcal F_m=1$ and $0$ distinguish the proved low- and high-temperature domains without a protecting symmetry. These sufficient domains do not determine the full phase diagram.

entry.title: Thermodynamic Stability of Classical $\mathbb Z_2$ Lattice Gauge Models
entry.summary: Finite-temperature phases are traditionally studied through spontaneous symmetry breaking, but symmetry-breaking fields can remove their distinction, as in the Ising model. This motivates the search for stable nontrivial thermal phases without symmetry protection. For classical $\mathbb Z_2$ lattice gauge models with spins on $m$-dimensional cells in a fixed spatial dimension $d$, we prove joint analyticity of the thermodynamic free-energy density in temperature and perturbation strength at sufficiently low positive temperatures under sufficiently weak local perturbations, whenever $1\le m\le d-2$. Perturbations need not preserve internal or gauge symmetries and may include noncommuting quantum interactions. A separate high-temperature expansion yields an analytic region reaching infinite temperature at any fixed finite perturbation strength. These results establish thermodynamic stability and support the conjecture that low- and high-temperature regimes remain separated by a thermal transition without symmetry protection.

entry.title: Mass Deformations and Sheets in Logahoric Higgs Moduli
entry.summary: We use the framework of the logahoric Hitchin integrable system introduced in our earlier work and the sheets of the Lie algebra in order to describe the tame defects in a six dimensional $\mathcal{N}=(2,0)$ superconformal theory under mass deformations. We show that varying leaves of fixed dimension in the Hitchin system amounts to varying residue orbits of fixed dimension. Moreover, we verify the period and dimension conditions in mass-like deformations, as proposed by Balasubramanian--Distler, thus realizing the sheets of the Lie algebra on the Poisson moduli space of logahoric Higgs torsors.

entry.title: Probing Minihalos in the Late Dark Ages through Velocity Acoustic Oscillations in the 21-cm Power Spectrum
entry.summary: In the Dark Ages, minihalos above the Jeans mass accrete gas from the intergalactic medium (IGM). The accreted gas would be heated to virial temperature and produces 21 cm signal in emission, while the majority of gas retained in the IGM is cold and has 21 cm signal in absorption. The 21 cm signal of the IGM generally dominates over that of minihalos, making it difficult to extract the contribution of minihalos from the detected 21 cm signal. However, in the late Dark Ages, in regions where the gas has not yet been influenced by the radiation from Pop III stars, the 21 cm signal from the IGM is weak because collisional coupling has become less efficient. More importantly, the relic supersonic dark matter-baryon relative streaming velocities suppress the gas accretion of smaller minihalos and encode their large-scale coherent features into the 21 cm signal, generating the velocity acoustic oscillation (VAO) features on the 21 cm power spectrum. This offers a promising avenue for detecting minihalos. We found that, at $z\sim 15$ ($\sim 20$), the first peak of the net VAO wiggle at $k=0.05$ Mpc$^{-1}$ is $\sim 1.4\times 10^{-3}$ ($\sim 3.1\times 10^{-4}$) mK$^2$. With a total of 24 lunar nights/8064 hr (60 lunar nights/20160 hr) of integration, the signal from $z\sim 15$ ($\sim 20$) is detectable for an array composed of 82944 (278784) dipoles, spread over $\sim 3.5$ ($\sim 6.3$) km. If the small-scale matter power spectrum is enhanced and minihalos are much more numerous than in the standard $Λ$CDM model, the signal is detectable for an even smaller scale array.

entry.title: The environments of type Ibn supernovae: evidence for a strong Wolf-Rayet star component
entry.summary: Characterisation of progenitor stars of supernovae (SNe) poses several challenges. Direct observations of progenitors are based on serendipitious archival observations and are only possible for nearby events. Indirect methods include inferring nickel mass from the light curves or oxygen masses from the SN's nebular phase, both of which are tools to constrain the progenitor's initial mass. Alternatively, environments of SNe have been used as a proxy for the progenitor's age and metallicity. The progenitor channel of type Ibn SNe is a hotly debated topic. The mass-loss and the formation of He-rich circumstellar medium requires strong envelope stripping of the progenitor star. For core-collapse supernovae (CCSNe), this requires strong stellar wind mass losses, i.e. a Wolf-Rayet (WR) star, or binary interaction with a companion star. Here, we analyse a sample of host galaxies of type Ibn SNe that have been observed with MUSE. We use H$α$ emission to infer the transient's association to star formation and derive the local metallicity with commonly used strong line diagnostic. We find that the sample of SNe are highly associated with star formation in the host galaxy, typically situated within one of the brightest HII regions in the host galaxy. The NCR distribution of H$α$ pixels in SN Ibn environments strongly resembles that of WR stars, and shows a stronger preference to SF compared to other core-collapse SN types. Metallicity measurements show typically sub-solar metallicity in the SN environments.

entry.title: Monodromy line defects on the fuzzy sphere
entry.summary: Monodromy line defects are of interest in the defect bootstrap program and are dual to electrically charged objects in dual gauge field descriptions. We investigate the Ising monodromy dCFT using a fuzzy sphere regularization, by imposing the twisted boundary condition in the UV. We obtain defect scaling dimensions $\hat Δ$ and ratios of defect operator expansion (DOE) coefficients using this method. We extend this machinery to the continuous family of $O(2)$ monodromy defects with twist angle $2πν$. In both cases, the lowest neutral defect scalar lies above dimension one, providing evidence that the monodromy defect reaches a stable dCFT without additional fine tuning.

entry.title: A bright X-ray flaring event from the intermediate supergiant fast X-ray transient IGR J00370+6122 observed with NuSTAR
entry.summary: We present an analysis of a long NuSTAR observation of the intermediate supergiant fast X-ray transient (SFXT) IGR J00370+6122, obtained around the peak of its orbital modulation. The observation has a net exposure ~93 ks. During the observation, the source displayed a bright flaring event that was resolved into numerous short flares with durations of 10-1000 s. The 3-70 keV luminosity spanned a dynamic range of ~200, from ~1E34 to ~1.8E36 erg/s; the maximum was reached for only ~40 s in total. The spectrum is well described by an absorbed double-Comptonisation model, with parameters consistent with those found in other X-ray pulsars accreting at similarly low luminosities. This is the first detection of a double-hump continuum in IGR J00370+6122, which extends this spectral state to the class of intermediate SFXTs. We searched for the previously reported ~346 s and ~674 s periodicities and find no significant signal at either period, which makes their interpretation as the neutron star spin period less likely. Using ~21 yr of Swift/BAT monitoring, we refine the orbital period of the system to P_orb=15.6654 +/- 0.0008 d. Finally, we discuss the observed flaring activity in the framework of quasi-spherical settling accretion, which is expected at the observed luminosities.

entry.title: The $m=2$ amplituhedron is a positive geometry
entry.summary: Amplituhedra are semi-algebraic sets of fundamental importance in particle physics. Their discovery initiated the field of Positive Geometry. We settle a central conjecture in this field: we show that the $m=2$ amplituhedron is a positive geometry. Our main new tool is a Hodge-theoretic criterion for being a positive geometry, connecting the work of Brown--Dupont with the original setup of Arkani-Hamed--Bai--Lam.

entry.title: Logarithmic corrections to massive particle trajectories for the classical soft log theorems at leading order in $G$
entry.summary: We study the logarithmic corrections to the asymptotic trajectories of massive particles. These corrections enter the calculation of the soft-log sector of the radiative field at null infinity in four-dimensional gravitational scattering. We first isolate the part of the metric which enters the particle equations of motion. We show that the nonlinear source can only affect this sector through homogeneous modes on the hyperboloid, and that matching to the proposed soft tower implies that these modes vanish, except for the first mode. We show that this mode cannot affect the trajectory coefficients at leading order in $G$. We then invert the matter energy-momentum tensor on the particle worldlines to obtain the trajectory coefficients at leading order in $G$ and at every logarithmic order using Legendre polynomials. The first two coefficients reproduce the known results at orders $G$ and $G^2$.

entry.title: Geometric Quantum Discord in Schwarzschild de Sitter Spacetime
entry.summary: We investigate geometric quantum discord for massless Dirac field modes in Schwarzschild-de Sitter spacetime, focusing on the distinct thermal effects of the black hole and cosmological horizons. For pure Bell-type and isotropic initial states, increasing the black hole mass at fixed cosmological constant restores accessible discord, while higher dimensionless frequencies favor its preservation. Inaccessible discord depends on the retained modes: higher frequencies suppress discord involving the inaccessible cosmological mode, whereas the frequency ordering reverses with increasing black hole mass for the inaccessible black hole mode paired with the accessible cosmological mode. For the selected parameters yielding equal initial discord, the two state families exhibit identical discord in sectors containing the inaccessible black hole mode but differ over part of the parameter range in the remaining inaccessible sector. At fixed positive dimensionless frequency, accessible discord returns to its initial value in the Nariai limit, while all three inaccessible discords vanish. These results reveal the interplay between horizon thermal effects, mode selection, and initial-state structure in shaping quantum correlations.

entry.title: Information Geometry of DGLAP Evolution: From Geodesic Tests to Emergent Small-Circle Geometry
entry.summary: We investigate the geometric structure of leading-order (LO) nonsinglet DGLAP evolution on the Fisher--Rao manifold of normalized valence distributions, asking whether the QCD-selected trajectory is geodesic and how its departure from geodesic motion is organized. Through the isometric embedding $Φ=2\sqrt{p}$, the evolution is represented as a curve on a Hilbert sphere of radius two, with its velocity and acceleration determined directly by the DGLAP operator. For a GRV98-based total-valence trajectory over $2\leq Q^2\leq 2000~{\rm GeV}^2$, we find a nonzero but weakly scale-dependent geodesic curvature. An arc-length-weighted principal-component analysis shows that two affine directions capture more than $99.999\%$ of the trajectory variance. The corresponding affine plane intersects the Fisher sphere in a small circle, whose predicted geodesic curvature closely agrees with that reconstructed from the DGLAP-generated acceleration. An $x$-resolved analysis further reveals that Fisher motion is governed by relative PDF reshaping rather than probability weight alone, with different momentum-fraction regions contributing to motion along the trajectory and its transverse bending. The Mellin representation provides a complementary perspective on the effective dimensional reduction through the collective evolution of the spectral hierarchy. These results establish a quantitative information-geometric characterization of the reference LO DGLAP trajectory and reveal an organized, near-small-circle structure over the finite evolution interval.

entry.title: Tunable state-dependent interactions in collisionally stable mixtures of polar molecules
entry.summary: We propose encoding a pseudo-spin-$1/2$ system in the ground ($v=0$) and first excited ($v=1$) vibrational states of polar molecules. Double microwave shielding simultaneously shields molecules in both states, suppressing two-body losses by orders of magnitude while strictly avoiding three-body recombination. The microwave dressing is state-dependent and results in highly tunable, long-range dipolar Ising exchange ($J_z$), density-density ($V$), and spin-density ($W$) interactions. These interaction length scales readily exceed the typical interparticle spacing, pushing the molecules deep into the strongly interacting regime. In bulk gases, this enables the exploration of itinerant quantum magnetism and quantum droplets with novel anisotropic spin textures; in optical lattices, it naturally realizes extended Hubbard and $t$-$J_z$ models, opening new directions in quantum simulation.

entry.title: Near-deterministic loading of molecular arrays by microwave-assisted collisions
entry.summary: Molecular tweezer arrays offer great prospects for quantum simulation, sensing, and computing, and would benefit from methods that enhance loading efficiency. Whereas light-assisted collisions underpin enhanced loading methods for atomic tweezer arrays, this approach cannot be directly extended to molecular arrays due to collisional loss. We show how this collisional loss can be suppressed by shelving molecules in rotationally or vibrationally excited states, so that a shelved molecule interacts with a newly loaded molecule through a repulsive van der Waals interaction. By introducing microwave assisted collisions, we show how to control the final states and the energy released in a collision between a pair of molecules. Following this controlled collision, one of the two molecules can be ejected, and we explore several strategies for ensuring deterministic ejection. Our schemes rely on currently available techniques for laser-coolable molecules, and we predict achievable filling fractions up to 96%, paving the way for scalable molecular arrays.

entry.title: Computing excited states of dipolar Bose--Einstein condensates by constrained gentlest ascent dynamics
entry.summary: Dipolar Bose--Einstein condensates (BECs), i.e., BECs with long-range dipole-dipole interactions (DDI), exhibit extraordinarily rich physics and serve as a versatile experimental platform for exploring exotic quantum states of matter. Within the mean-field framework, a dipolar BEC can be described by the Gross--Pitaevskii (GP) model with a DDI term. Its stationary states consist of the ground state, which minimizes the GP energy functional under the normalization constraint, and excited states, which are higher-energy critical points that typically correspond to constrained saddle points. Excited states encode collective excitation modes and play a key role in the dynamical stability and quantum phase transitions of cold-atom systems. However, in contrast to the extensively studied ground state, they remain far less explored numerically, especially in dipolar systems. In this work, we develop a numerical method based on the constrained gentlest ascent dynamics (CGAD) that systematically computes excited states of dipolar BECs by stably targeting constrained saddle points with any prescribed Morse index. Specifically, a semi-implicit sine-pseudospectral discretization with an orthonormalization correction step is adopted, and the nonlocal DDI terms are evaluated efficiently and accurately via the nonuniform fast Fourier transform (NUFFT). The resulting scheme is applied to one-, two-, and three-dimensional dipolar BECs, enabling a detailed numerical investigation of their excited states. Remarkably, our simulations reveal that excited states can persist even in regimes where the ground state of the condensate becomes mean-field unstable. This work provides a computational framework for studying excited states in dipolar quantum gases and offers insights for future theoretical and experimental investigations.

entry.title: Complete Relational Description of Spin in a Quantum Background
entry.summary: The standard description of the state of a spin in quantum mechanics presupposes externally fixed directions -- a classical background. Can a spin be fully described instead in relation to other quantum mechanical systems? Poulin suggested twenty years ago group averaging over rotations the joint state of a fundamental spin and a reference spin with large angular momentum which, however, yields a classical bit in a probabilistic mixture. We revisit this idea and show that when the quantum reference system is augmented to \emph{two} large spins, the standard quantum mechanical description of a spin is recovered in the limit of large quantum numbers for the reference system.

entry.title: Gravitational-wave responses and noise correlations in geometric time-delay interferometry
entry.summary: Space-based gravitational-wave observations will probe the formation and growth of massive black holes and the evolution of compact binaries in the millihertz band. We develop a geometric-link representation of time-delay interferometry using six round-trip and six non-round-trip two-link blocks. Starting from the one-way Doppler response, we derive the elementary block responses and a dictionary that expresses 45 known second-generation combinations in terms of these blocks and residual one-way measurements. Representative Michelson and Relay observables admit compact forms, from which analytical sky-averaged tensor responses are obtained for a fixed, equal-arm constellation. We also derive the noise covariance of the blocks, retaining cross-spectra between blocks that share measurement streams. The resulting noise spectra agree with direct one-way assembly. We apply this formulation to a narrowband compact-binary signal in an equal-arm LISA instrument model. For the Relay example, neglecting the shared-link cross-spectrum changes the low-frequency noise scaling and overestimates the conditional Fisher uncertainties in amplitude or distance by factors of 10.71 at 1~mHz and 3.37 at 3~mHz.

entry.title: Carrollian Yang-Mills theories in the homogeneous temporal gauge
entry.summary: We quantize, in the homogeneous temporal gauge, both the electric and the magnetic Carrollian Yang-Mills theories with SU(N) gauge symmetry in the fundamental representation. We use the BRST method implemented in the path integral. We show that in the first case all the interaction vertices vanish, thus, giving a free theory. In the magnetic case, there are no loop contributions to the Green functions of the elementary fields --i.e., Green functions not involving composite operators-- and the only connected parts of such Green functions with a dependence on the coupling constant are the tree level contributions to the three and four point functions of the field $ξ_i$. We also show that in the magnetic case the Green functions involving only Wilson loops are trivial and not so in the electric case.

entry.title: Free-field realizations of $\mathcal{N} = 1$ supersymmetric $\mathcal{W}$-algebras associated with Lie superalgebras $B (n - 1 , n)$ and $B (n , n)$
entry.summary: We extend the recursive construction of free-field realizations proposed by Ide, Ito, and Miyazaki to the $\mathcal{N} = 1$ supersymmetric $\mathcal{W}$-algebras $\mathcal{SW} B (n - 1 , n)$ and $\mathcal{SW} B (n , n)$, associated with the Lie superalgebras $B (n - 1 , n)$ and $B (n , n)$, respectively. We obtain explicit free-field realizations of $\mathcal{SW} B (0 , 1)$, $\mathcal{SW} B (1 , 1)$, $\mathcal{SW} B (1 , 2)$, and $\mathcal{SW} B (2 , 2)$. In particular, the realizations of $\mathcal{SW} B (1 , 2)$ and $\mathcal{SW} B (2 , 2)$ are new. Using these realizations, we compute central charges, conformal weights, and eigenvalues of the generating currents on free-field highest-weight states, and construct the local integrals of motion $I_1$, $I_3$, and $I_5$.

entry.title: Unveiling dark forces with measurements of the Large Scale Structure of the Universe
entry.summary: Cosmology offers opportunities to test Dark Matter independently of its interactions with the Standard Model. We study the imprints of long-range forces acting solely in the dark sector on the distribution of galaxies, the so-called Large Scale Structure (LSS). We derive the strongest constraint on such forces from a combination of Planck and BOSS data. Along the way we consistently develop, for the first time, the Effective Field Theory of LSS in the presence of new dynamics in the dark sector. We forecast that future surveys will improve the current bound by an order of magnitude.

entry.title: Probing freeze-in dark matter using Bose-Einstein condensate in neutron star
entry.summary: Neutron star (NS) is one of the most promising astrophysical targets to probe non-gravitational interaction of dark matter (DM) with visible matter. Their compactness makes them an ideal object which can capture particle DM efficiently over its lifetime using the DM-nucleon scattering cross-section. If DM particles are bosonic, then the captured DM population may form a Bose-Einstein condensate at the center of the NS, increasing the DM density significantly. In this work, we study the phenomenology of such scenario with enhanced DM annihilation rate due to the increased density in a condensate. The enhanced DM annihilation makes the NS surface `hotter' than in the standard cooling scenario. We show that the annihilation rate is enhanced by a factor of $\mathcal{O}(10^{15}-10^{20})$ if DM forms a condensate without large self-interaction, and DM with freeze-in value annihilation cross-section can heat up the NS to higher temperatures, bringing it within the reach of James Webb Space Telescope. It also allows us to probe DM-nucleon scattering cross section within the neutrino fog regime which will complement the terrestrial direct detection searches. Moreover, the enhanced annihilation from the condensate changes the lower limits on s-wave DM annihilation cross-section for capture-annihilation equilibrium and the formation of a black hole inside the NS. Finally, we show an example of a scalar DM model where such small annihilation and DM-nucleon scattering cross sections can generically arise.

entry.title: Inflationary Particle Production and the Swampland
entry.summary: We investigate the impact of particle production during inflation in scenarios where an infinite tower of states features a mass scale that decreases exponentially along the inflationary trajectory. Such couplings naturally arise in string effective field theories and are in fact motivated by the Swampland Distance Conjecture (SDC). We show that the corrections to inflationary observables sourced by the tower scale as $(H/Λ_{\text{sp}})^{2+p}$, with $H$ being the Hubble scale, $Λ_{\text{sp}}$ being the species scale, that is the quantum gravity cut-off, and $p\geq 1$ characterizes the density of states in the tower. As a result, in gravitationally weakly coupled cosmological effective theories, the tower-induced contributions are suppressed relative to the standard single-field predictions, leaving the inflationary phenomenology essentially unchanged. We demonstrate this explicitly across a set of well-motivated inflationary potentials, and we compare the resulting predictions with the most recent observational constraints, including those from the Atacama Cosmology Telescope.

entry.title: Thermodynamic Supercritical Scaling Law for the charged Gauss-Bonnet AdS Black Hole
entry.summary: The phase structure of the charged Gauss-Bonnet AdS black holes varies with the spacetime dimension. Within an appropriate parameter range, only the six-dimensional case admits two physical critical points and it is an ideal model for investigating supercritical thermodynamics in black hole systems with multiple critical points. In this study, we investigate the supercritical thermodynamic properties of this model in the extended phase space and construct the supercritical phase diagrams associated with the two critical points. The thermodynamic supercritical scaling analysis for the supercritical crossover lines in the vicinity of both critical points is completed, demonstrating universality. The corresponding coefficients for the external field scaling and the order parameter scaling are obtained, and their physical significance is discussed.

entry.title: Universal electrical resistivity in iron-based high-temperature superconductors
entry.summary: Temperature-dependent electrical resistivity $ρ(T)$ in cuprate, iron-based, and nickelate superconductors represents one of unresolved problems in modern solid-state physics, because of the high absolute value of $ρ(T)$, which, in many cases, exceeds the Ioffe-Rigel criterion, and a large difference in the $ρ(T)$ shape for samples with different doping. Here I show that the nearest neighbors parallel resistivity model (arXiv: 2607.23484) can well describe the in-plane resistivity $ρ_{ab}(T)$ in iron-based superconductors (IBS) of type 11, 111, 122, 1111, 1144 and 42214 in which the spin density wave phase or nematic order is suppressed by doping. The model is based on the postulate that $ρ_{ab}(T)$ is a sum of two parallel conduction channels, where one channel is described by the Bloch-Grüneisen equation and the other by the Arrhenius hopping equation. Consequently, the variety of $ρ_{ab}(T)$ in the IBS is explained as a variation of the Debye temperature $Θ_D$ and the hopping activation energy $E_a$. The derived Debye temperatures were used to estimate the electron-phonon coupling constant $λ_{e-ph}$in the studied IBS.

entry.title: Luther-Emery liquid in one-dimensional attractive Fermi gas
entry.summary: One-dimensional (1D) interacting Fermi gases underpin a rich variety of quantum liquids, ranging from the Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid and the Fulde-Ferrell-Larkin-Ovchinnikov paired state to the Luther-Emery liquid (LEL). Notably, the LEL-characterized by gapless excitations in charge or spin degree of freedom and gapped excitations in the other-has long been theoretically predicted but has eluded definitive experimental observation to date. By exactly solving the attractive Yang-Gaudin model via the Bethe ansatz, we fully determine the low-energy excitation spectra for both spin and charge channels. For fully paired fermions, the spectrum features gapped spin excitation coexisting with gapless charge excitation. We further employ bosonization to derive analytical expressions for the dynamical structure factor (DSF) of the gapped spin excitation, which is a long-standing challenge in this study. In the trapped gas, we find that the spin Bragg spectroscopy peak occurs at a much higher frequency than the charge-mode peak, where the splitting frequency between these two peaks scales approximately linearly with the interaction strength. Crucially, the spin gap manifests as a sharp threshold in the spin DSF, below which spectral weight is completely absent, proving a direct and unambiguous spectroscopic fingerprint of the LEL. Our work establishes quasi-1D trapped attractive Fermi gases as a pristine experimental platform for the long-sought direct observation of the LEL.

entry.title: Exact 1D Nonlinear Solutions for Proton-Driven Plasma Wakefields
entry.summary: We extend the classical 1D nonlinear relativistic plasma wakefield paradigm to evaluate the pristine fluid profiles driven by intense relativistic proton trains under the comoving coordinate approximation. Using an intense two-bunch scheme, our adaptive integration model is validated down to machine precision against exact closed-form cold-fluid invariants, confirming that interface boundary corners represent physical step discontinuities in the second potential derivative. Scaling to an $N=100$ micro-bunch train, we resolve macroscopic phase-accumulation and subsequent nonlinear detuning by deriving a closed-form, parameter-free piecewise analytical envelope expression. This solution successfully maps the initial unattenuated quadratic coherent growth alongside the flat asymptotic horizontal saturation horizon governed by nonlinear energy conservation. Furthermore, the framework analytically evaluates the transient envelope overshoot, tracking its decay onto the saturation boundary via an exact phase-slip integration length scale. Providing immediate, ready macro-envelope bounds, this computationally inexpensive tool eliminates empirical adjustments and yields a robust mathematical baseline designed to guide and accelerate complex, multi-dimensional particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations through rapid parameter space exploration before deploying heavy computational assets. It establishes an efficient foundation to optimize asymmetric, custom-shaped driver profiles required to break the fundamental symmetric transformer ratio limit of 2 to make current particle accelerators more efficient.

entry.title: What Shapes the Ultraviolet Spectra of Type Ia Supernovae?
entry.summary: Ultraviolet (UV) observations of Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) exhibit significant diversity, but their physical origin remains poorly understood. We investigate UV spectra of SNe Ia observed with the Swift UltraViolet and Optical Telescope. Our expanded pre-maximum sample probes dependencies on decline rate, ejecta properties, and host environment. We recover the correlation between UV flux and decline rate near maximum in the near-UV (NUV), and find correlations at pre-maximum phases in both the NUV and mid-UV (MUV). This trend is strongly wavelength dependent, with slow decliners showing higher NUV but lower MUV flux than fast decliners. Synthetic TARDIS spectra varying the 56Ni abundance show that enhanced 56Ni suppresses the MUV while increasing the NUV, broadly reproducing the trend. We find no significant correlation between UV flux and ejecta velocity, while Si II 6355 pEW shows trends similar to those with decline rate. We also find no significant correlations with host-galaxy properties, although host environment may contribute to the remaining UV diversity among SNe with similar decline rates. Early-excess SNe show enhanced flux mainly in the NUV rather than a broad UV excess, suggesting that strong circumstellar interaction is not necessarily required to explain the observed excess emission. Peculiar subclasses show distinct UV properties, with brighter and hotter subclasses showing higher UV flux, although the current sample is small and does not cover all SN Ia subtypes. Our results suggest that the UV diversity of SNe Ia is shaped by multiple mechanisms that contribute differently across the UV wavelength range.

entry.title: Causality and perturbative-QCD constraints on first-order phase transitions in neutron stars
entry.summary: Causality bounds the compactness and maximum mass of neutron stars. We generalise this bound to equations of state (EOSs) with a first-order phase transition between maximally stiff phases. In units of the transition energy density, the problem depends only on $q=\ptr/\etr$ and $j=Δ\ve/\etr$. The maximum compactness equals the smooth value $\mathcal{C}=0.354$ for $q\to0$ or $j\to0$, is unaffected for $q\gtrsim0.67$, and is otherwise reduced by typically $\lesssim0.04$ when the maximum-mass star is a hybrid star and by up to $0.13$ when it is the last hadronic star. Matching to a Baym--Pethick--Sutherland crust and a chiral-EFT polytrope at $n_m=1.1\,n_0$ and inverting the bound, no causal EOS supports $2.01\,\Msun$ if the energy-density jump exceeds $\simeq460$--$495~{\rm MeV\,fm^{-3}}$. Additionally, imposing radius constraint of $R\ge11.6$~km it shrinks to $\simeq235$--$395~{\rm MeV\,fm^{-3}}$. These limits hold whatever the matter above the transition, for onsets within $\simeq0.2\,n_0$ of $n_m$. Relaxing maximal stiffness, we build EOSs with a transition at $μ_{\rm tr}=1000$--$1300$~MeV, matched to perturbative QCD (pQCD) at $2.6$~GeV. pQCD limits the jump; EOSs compatible with PSR J0740+6620, J1614$-$2230, J0437$-$4715, J0614$-$3329, GW170817, and XTE J1814-338 appear only at $μ_{\rm tr}=1200$ and $1250$~MeV; and inside the causal window, the largest jump agrees with the bound within the grid resolution. Finally, inserting a transition at $2.01\,\Msun$ into hadronic EOSs that satisfy five pulsar observations, the EOS with the lowest break density gives a narrow stable hybrid window ($ΔM\simeq0.005\,\Msun$), compatible with XTE J1814-338 for jumps of $6$--$8\,n_0$ and with pQCD; three EOSs with higher break densities give none.

entry.title: Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid theory for one-dimensional attractive Fermi gases
entry.summary: The one-dimensional (1D) Yang-Gaudin model--an integrable $δ$-function interacting Fermi gas, serves as a paradigm in quantum many-body physics, encompassing phenomena from spin-charge separation to the Luther-Emery liquid. However, a consistent description of the Luther-Emery liquid and the Fulde-Ferrell-Larkin-Ovchinnikov (FFLO)-like pairing states in the 1D attractive Fermi gas remains elusive. In this work, we develop a universal Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid (TLL) theory to describe the FFLO state both for the case of weak and strong binding between fermions of opposite spins. We rigorously derive a low-energy effective Hamiltonian using bosonization, revealing the emergence of a two-component TLL: one exhibiting spin-charge coupling in the weak binding regime, and another featuring charge-charge separation in the strong binding regime. For the weak binding regime, we further derive renormalization-group equations for the sine-Gordon term in the spin sector and show that this term undergoes a relevant-irrelevant phase transition driven by the magnetic field. We further analyze the dynamical correlation functions of the FFLO pairing state based on the effective Hamiltonian we constructed. Finally, we discuss experiments using ultracold atoms to elucidate the Luther-Emery liquid behavior and the subtle phenomena of spin-charge coupling and charge-charge separation.

entry.title: Suppression and reemergence of directional transport across the ferromagnetic transition in SrRuO$_3$
entry.summary: SrRuO$_3$ is a canonical itinerant ferromagnet that continues to serve as a fertile platform for exploring spin-orbit coupled transport and topological responses in correlated oxide metals. Here, we investigate a (110)-oriented epitaxial SrRuO3 thin film on DyScO$_3$, where crystallographic anisotropy allows for symmetry-resolved charge transport along orthogonal in-plane directions. We uncover two principal findings. First, the resistance above the Curie temperature $T_{c,on}\approx 165$ K exhibits strong anisotropy, consistent with directionally dependent spin-fluctuation scattering. Below $T_{c,on}$, this anisotropy nearly vanishes, despite persistent structural inequivalence, due to isotropic electron-magnon and electron-electron scattering processes. Second, the application of a magnetic field reveals a striking directional contrast in the linear magnetoresistance (MR): it remains negative and saturates along [001], but changes sign and becomes positive along $[1\bar{1}0]$ below $T_0=145$ K. In contrast, the quadratic MR term is identical for both directions and peaks near $T_{\mathrm{OHE}}^*=155$ K, where the ordinary Hall coefficient crosses zero, consistent with carrier compensation under a two-band scenario. A sign change in the anomalous Hall signal at $T_{\mathrm{AHE}}^*=150$ K is consistent with a temperature-dependent redistribution of Berry-curvature contributions near the Fermi level. These results establish ferromagnetic ordering as the primary driver of the observed directional magnetotransport in SrRuO$_3$.

entry.title: Non-Coulomb $Q$-cohomology and quantum lifting
entry.summary: We study quantum lifting of classical BPS cohomology classes in four-dimensional $\mathcal N=4$ super-Yang-Mills theory. Certain powers of the gaugino bilinear $\mathcal S=\text{Tr}(λ_+λ_-)$ in orthogonal theories provide non-Coulomb monotones: multi-graviton classes that vanish upon Cartan restriction. For $SO(7)$, we identify $\mathcal S^4$ as a superconformal descendant of a known lifted monotone class, explaining the latter's non-Coulomb character, and explicitly construct a fortuitous lifting partner for $\mathcal S^4$. This construction provides a strategy for finding analogous partners for higher powers at higher ranks. Our main result establishes restrictions on the quantum lifting of classical BPS cohomologies for general gauge groups. We show that the one-loop correction $Q_1$ to the supercharge annihilates every monotone class in classical cohomology, while every non-zero $Q_1$ image is of non-Coulomb type. Thus every non-zero one-loop pairing has a fortuitous source and a non-Coulomb target, so that Coulomb monotones survive at this order at finite rank. In the BMN sector, our results imply that non-Coulomb monotones survive at one loop order as well. A crucial step in the argument shows that every non-Coulomb class, fortuitous or monotone, is annihilated in classical cohomology by a sufficiently high power of a scalar discriminant, which we interpret as a partial no-hair property.
